definitions.gloss: oneself (emphatic, following a noun or pronoun)
definitions.explanation: Attaches directly to a person word or pronoun to stress that this very person, and no one else, is meant: {私|わたし}{自身|じしん} (I myself), {社長|しゃちょう}{自身|じしん} (the president himself). It does not stand alone as a subject.

examples.japanese: {私|わたし}{自身|じしん}も{驚|おどろ}いた。
それは{彼|かれ}{自身|じしん}が{決|き}めたことだ。
examples.english: That is something he decided himself.

examples.japanese: {選手|せんしゅ}{自身|じしん}が{引退|いんたい}を{決|き}めたと、{監督|かんとく}が{記者|きしゃ}{会見|かいけん}で{説明|せつめい}した。
examples.english: The manager explained at a press conference that the player himself had decided to retire.

notes:
{自身|じしん} follows the word it emphasizes with no particle in between. It is used with people; for a thing or an abstract noun, Japanese uses {自体|じたい} instead ({制度|せいど}{自体|じたい}, the system itself).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {私|わたし}{自身|じしん}: I myself
- {自分|じぶん}{自身|じしん}: one's own self (a very common doubled form)
- {自身|じしん}の{経験|けいけん}: one's own experience
- {自身|じしん}で{確|たし}かめる: to check for oneself

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {自分|じぶん}: oneself — can stand alone as a subject or object; {自身|じしん} cannot
- {自|みずか}ら: personally, of one's own accord — an adverb stressing that one acted without being told
